method: Rebuild from primary text. Every section of the Freelance Worker Protection Act — Bus. & Prof. Code §§18100, 18101, 18102, 18103, 18104, 18105, 18106 and 18107 — was fetched from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and read, together with Lab. Code §2778(b)(2), which supplies the definition of 'professional services' that §18101(c) adopts. CourtListener was searched for construing decisions and none was found. Assertions describe the REBUILT body.
queries: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§18100-18107 full text (leginfo)
"Freelance Worker Protection Act" freelance worker written contract

assertions.text: the Act reaches only 'professional services' as defined in Lab. Code §2778(b)(2), which is a closed list
assertions.note: §18101(c): '"Professional services" has the same meaning as paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) of Section 2778 of the Labor Code.' That paragraph runs from (A) to (O) and enumerates specific occupations, several with their own conditions. The previous body applied the Act to 'an individual freelancer' with no limit on the kind of work. This is the largest defect in the clause and nobody had recorded it: the clause asserted the Act over engagements it does not reach.

assertions.text: a freelance worker is a person or an organisation of no more than one person, retained as a bona fide independent contractor, for $250 or more counting all contracts between the same parties in the immediately preceding 120 days
assertions.note: §18101(a), verbatim. The 120-day aggregation was already in the clause's defect list and is now in the body. 'Organization composed of no more than one person, whether or not incorporated or employing a trade name' is broader than 'individual' and the previous body missed it.

assertions.text: the hiring party excludes the United States government, the State of California or a subdivision, a foreign government, and an individual hiring for personal, family or homestead purposes
the contract must be in writing, a signed copy furnished physically or electronically, and retained for no less than four years
assertions.note: §18103(a), verbatim. The signed copy was in the clause's defect list; the retention period the previous body had was right.

assertions.text: the required contract contents are the four items in §18103(b)
assertions.note: §18103(b)(1)-(4): name and MAILING ADDRESS of each party; an itemised list of all services INCLUDING the value of those services and the rate and method of compensation; the payment date or the mechanism for determining it; and the date by which the freelancer must submit a list of services rendered to meet the hiring party's internal processing deadlines. The previous body had 'the parties' rather than names and mailing addresses.

assertions.text: payment is due on the contract date, or within 30 days of completion if none is specified

once work has begun, the hiring party may not require, as a condition of timely payment, acceptance of less compensation OR the provision of more goods or services or the grant of more intellectual property rights than agreed
assertions.note: §18102(b)(1)-(2). The previous body had only the first prong. The second matters in an IP assignment context, which is what a contractor agreement is.

assertions.text: anti-retaliation covers four protected activities and uses a 'reasonably likely to deter' standard
any waiver is void and unenforceable

remedies: attorney's fees, costs and injunctive relief to a prevailing plaintiff; $1,000 for a refused written contract that was requested; up to twice the unpaid amount for late payment; the value of the contract or the work for any other violation
assertions.note: §18106(a)-(b). The previous body stated no remedy at all, which for a clause whose whole point is to keep a hiring party out of trouble is a strange omission.

assertions.text: the Act does not displace ordinary contract law and an oral contract remains enforceable
assertions.note: §18103(c), which also lists three kinds of evidence that a contract was formed notwithstanding a refusal to sign one.

assertions.text: the Act applies only to contracts entered into or renewed on or after January 1, 2025
assertions.note: §18107, verbatim. Absent from the previous body.

priorDefects: citation-gap: the only citation was 'Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §18100 (SB 988)'. §18100 reads in full: 'This part shall be known, and may be cited, as the Freelance Worker Protection Act.' Every operative rule in the clause was cited to a section containing none of it.
overstated-scope: the clause applied the Act to any 'individual freelancer'. It reaches only the closed list of professional services in Lab. Code §2778(b)(2).
omitted: the 120-day aggregation of the $250 threshold.
omitted: the requirement to furnish a signed copy.
omitted: the prohibition on conditioning payment on more goods, services or IP rights.
omitted: the anti-waiver provision and every remedy in §18106.
omitted: that a single-person organisation, incorporated or not, is a freelance worker.
gaps: The 'professional services' list has conditions inside it — marketing must be original and creative work depending primarily on the individual's invention, imagination or talent; freelance writing and the licensed trades have multi-part tests; the still photographer and content contributor entries have their own limits. The rebuilt clause names representative categories and says the list is closed but does not reproduce the conditions, so a hiring party still cannot tell from the clause whether a particular engagement is inside it.
No decision construing §§18100-18107 was found on CourtListener. The Act took effect on 1 January 2025 and appears entirely unconstrued.

Whether a pre-2025 contract amended after that date comes within the Act was not resolved. §18107 says 'entered into or renewed', which is narrower than the 'entered into, modified, or extended' formula other California statutes use — including Lab. Code §925(f) in this same corpus.
How §18106's damages interact with an ordinary breach claim for the same unpaid amount was not researched.
